item.title: Inside our new Git storage — built for agents & humans
item.dc:creator: Karthik Example
item.description:
Our new Git storage architecture lets thousands of agents push to a single repository at once — here’s how we built it, what broke, and what we’d do differently. We cover replication, consensus, and the performance work that made it fast enough for every developer on the platform, with plenty of detail on the trade-offs we made along the way and the benchmarks we ran before shipping it to everyone.

The post Inside our new Git storage appeared first on The Example Blog.
item.content:encoded:
Git hosting at scale is mostly a distributed systems problem. We built on git/git and our own spokes-lite. See also the tracking issue, #git on GitHub, sponsors, a gist, and the REST docs.

Replication and consensus details follow.

item.title: The post-quantum future of web privacy
item.description: Cryptographic protocols keep sites safe from abuse while keeping users private. Here is how we are moving them to post-quantum cryptography.
item.content:encoded: The highest priorities for the post-quantum transition are the basics. Our reference implementation lives at https://github.com/example/pq-privacy-pass.
